ing: whole leaves, or fresh cabbage leaves blanched
diced, plus extra slices to layer
st: Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onions and diced bacon for 8 minutes until soft. Cool for 10 minutes.
In a bowl mix the pork, rice, onion mixture, dill, paprika, thyme, pepper and [[1 tsp]] salt well.
Trim the thick rib off each cabbage leaf. Place about [[3 tbsp]] filling at the base of a leaf, fold in the sides and roll up snugly.
Line the bottom of a heavy pot with torn leaves and a few bacon slices. Pack the rolls in tightly, seam side down, and tuck in the bay leaves.
Mix the crushed tomatoes, [[2 cups]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt, then pour over the rolls so they are just covered. Put a plate on top to weigh them down.
Bring to a boil, then cover and cook in a 350°F (175°C) oven or on very low heat for 2 hours 15 minutes.
Check that the pork inside is at least 160°F (71°C). Rest for 15 minutes.
Serve hot with sour cream and polenta.
Bring [[5 cups]] water and the salt to a boil in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Lower the heat and slowly pour in the cornmeal in a thin stream, whisking constantly to prevent lumps.
Switch to a wooden spoon and cook on low heat, stirring often, for 25 minutes until it pulls away from the sides of the pot.
Stir in the butter and taste for salt.
Turn the mămăligă out onto a board or plate and shape it into a mound. Let it set 3 minutes.
Cut with a string or knife into thick slices.
Serve warm, topped with the crumbled cheese and sour cream.
Put the beef and pork in a large bowl and add the garlic, thyme, paprika, pepper and salt.
Dissolve the baking soda in the cold broth and add it to the meat.
Knead the mixture by hand for 5 to 8 minutes until very sticky and well blended.
Cover and chill the meat for at least 1 hour, or overnight, so the flavors develop.
With wet hands, shape small portions into fat fingers about 3 inches long and 1 inch thick, without a casing.
Grill over medium-high heat, or broil, for 10 to 12 minutes, turning often, until browned and at least 160°F (71°C) inside.
Serve at once with mustard and bread.
Put the tripe in a large pot, cover with cold water, bring to a boil for 10 minutes, then drain and rinse. This removes the strong smell.
Return the tripe to the pot with [[10 cups]] fresh water and the bay leaves. Boil, then simmer for 2 hours 30 minutes until very tender.
Lift out the tripe, cut it into thin strips, and return it to the broth.
Add the carrots, onion, celery root and salt and simmer for 25 minutes until tender.
Mash the garlic with [[1 tbsp]] vinegar to make a garlic-vinegar mix.
In a bowl whisk the sour cream, egg yolks and flour. Slowly whisk in 2 ladles of hot broth to temper it.
Pour this mixture into the pot off the heat, stirring, and warm for 3 minutes without boiling. The eggs get hot but must not curdle.
Stir in the remaining [[2 tbsp]] vinegar, serve with the garlic mix and chilies on the side.

ing: for a sour taste, to adjust
st: Mix the pork, rice, egg, half of the onion, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper by hand until sticky. Roll into 1-inch meatballs.
Heat the oil in a pot and cook the remaining onion, carrots and bell pepper for 6 minutes.
Add [[8 cups]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt and bring to a boil.
Add the tomato puree and simmer for 10 minutes.
Gently drop in the meatballs one by one. Simmer for 25 minutes until the rice is cooked and the meatballs reach 160°F (71°C).
Stir in the lovage, then add lemon juice a little at a time until it is pleasantly sour.
Sprinkle with dill and serve with sour cream and hot pepper if you like.
Heat the lard in a heavy pot and brown the pork in batches for 10 minutes. Add the onion and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and wine and scrape up the brown bits, then add [[1 tsp]] salt, the pepper and enough water to just cover the meat.
Cover and simmer for 45 minutes until the pork is tender and at least 145°F (63°C).
Add the sausage and garlic and cook uncovered for 10 minutes until the sauce is thick.
Meanwhile boil [[5 cups]] water with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and whisk in the cornmeal, then cook it, stirring, for 20 minutes into thick polenta.
Fry the eggs in a nonstick pan until the whites are set and the yolks are as runny as you like.
Serve the stew over polenta with a fried egg and feta on each portion.

ing: peeled and chopped, or 1 can crushed
st: Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C). Roast the whole peppers and eggplants on a lined sheet for 40 minutes, turning, until charred and collapsed.
Put the peppers in a covered bowl for 10 minutes, then peel and seed them. Peel the eggplants, draining off any bitter juices.
Chop the peppers and eggplant very finely, or pulse in a food processor to a thick rough puree.
Cook the onion in [[0.25 cup]] of the oil in a wide pot for 10 minutes until golden.
Add the tomatoes and tomato paste and cook 10 minutes.
Add the pepper-eggplant mixture, the remaining oil, bay leaves, salt, pepper and sugar.
Simmer over low heat for 50 minutes, stirring often, until very thick and glossy and no liquid pools on the surface.
Cool, remove the bay leaves and store in clean jars in the fridge for up to 2 weeks. Serve on bread.
Char the whole eggplants directly over a gas flame, under a hot broiler, or on a grill, turning, for 20 to 25 minutes until the skin is black and the flesh is very soft.
Place them in a colander for 15 minutes to drain the bitter juices.
Peel off the skin, and scrape off any bits of burned skin from the flesh.
Chop the flesh finely with a wooden or plastic knife on a board for about 5 minutes into a fine paste. Avoid metal, which can darken it.
Place the paste in a bowl. Add the lemon juice, salt and pepper and stir.
Whisk in the oil a spoonful at a time, stirring in one direction, until creamy and pale.
Fold in the onion, chill for 30 minutes, and serve with tomato slices and bread.
Mash the cheese in a bowl until smooth and stir in the eggs, sugar, lemon zest, vanilla and salt.
Mix the flour and baking powder, then fold into the cheese until you get a soft dough that is only slightly sticky. Add 1 tablespoon more flour if too wet.
Rest the dough for 10 minutes.
With floured hands, shape a large ball for each doughnut, with a small ball on top and make a hole in the middle with your finger. Or just make plain rings.
Heat the oil to 340°F (170°C) in a deep pot.
Fry the doughnuts in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden and cooked through. Drain on paper towels.
Top each warm doughnut with a large spoonful of sour cream and jam and serve right away.
Mix the warm milk, [[1 tbsp]] sugar and the yeast. Let it sit for 10 minutes until foamy.
In a large bowl mix the flour, remaining sugar and salt. Add the foamy yeast milk, the 2 eggs, 1 egg yolk, vanilla and lemon zest.
Knead for 5 minutes, then knead in the softened butter piece by piece for 5 more minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let the dough rise in a warm place for 1.5 hours until doubled.
For the filling, mix the walnuts, cocoa and brown sugar with the [[0.5 cup]] hot milk to a thick paste. Cool.
Divide the dough in half. Roll each piece into a rectangle, spread with filling, roll up tightly and twist the roll. Place in two greased loaf pans.
Cover and rise for 45 minutes. Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C), brush with the other yolk beaten with a little milk, and bake for 40 to 45 minutes until deep golden.
Cool in the pans for 15 minutes before slicing.
Rinse the offal, then boil it in salted water for 15 minutes. Drain and cool.
Chop the cooked offal very finely or pulse in a food processor until coarse but cohesive.
Hard-boil 2 eggs for 10 minutes, cool, peel, and set aside whole.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a loaf pan with the butter.
Squeeze the bread so it is damp and mix it with the offal, 2 raw eggs, green onions, dill, parsley, salt and pepper.
Put half the mixture in the pan, press the whole boiled eggs in a line down the middle, then cover with the rest.
Bake for 45 to 50 minutes until firm and an inside temperature of 160°F (71°C) is reached.
Cool 15 minutes, then slice. Serve warm or cold with green onions and bread.
